newsitem.title: Austria: ALPINE SKIING-FIRST WOMEN'S WORLD CUP DOWNHILL CALLED OFF.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-FIRST WOMEN'S WORLD CUP DOWNHILL CALLED OFF.

text.p: The first of two women's World Cup downhill races at this Austrian resort had to be called off on Saturday because of heavy fog.
Organisers were forced to halt the race after nine skiers had completed their runs. They hope the second downhill, scheduled here for 1315 local time (1215 GMT), could still go ahead.

World Cup officials had scheduled two downhills for Saturday after fog had forced them to halt one race on Friday after seven racers. Friday's race was itself meant to be the replacement for a downhill which had to be called off in Crans Montana, Switzerland, in December.
Austria's Stefanie Schuster was leading on the 3,010-metre long Strohsack piste before the interruption with a time of one minute 43.49 seconds.
Germany's Katarina Gutensohn was lying second in 1:44.00, ahead of compatriot Miriam Vogt in 1:44.01.
